from vulture import cache, core


def scan(paths, cache_dir, **kwargs):
    vulture = core.Vulture(cache_dir=cache_dir, **kwargs)
    vulture.scavenge(paths)
    return vulture


def write_files(root, files):
    for filename, source in files.items():
        path = root / filename
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(source)


def test_cache_path_helpers(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    relative = tmp_path / "directory" / ".." / "Example.py"
    assert cache.get_cache_path(tmp_path) == tmp_path / "cache.json"
    assert Path(cache.normalize_path(relative)).is_absolute()

    monkeypatch.setattr(cache.sys, "platform", "win32")
    assert cache.normalize_path(relative).endswith("example.py")


def test_unchanged_modules_are_reused_and_dependents_are_invalidated(tmp_path):
    write_files(
        tmp_path,
        {
            "a.py": "import b\na = 1\n",
            "b.py": "import c\nb = 1\n",
            "c.py": "c = 1\n",
            "unrelated.py": "unrelated = 1\n",
        },
    )
    cache_dir = tmp_path / ".cache"
    all_paths = {
        cache.normalize_path(tmp_path / filename)
        for filename in ("a.py", "b.py", "c.py", "unrelated.py")
    }

    first = scan([tmp_path], cache_dir)
    assert first._cache_stats == {"scanned": all_paths, "reused": set()}

    second = scan([tmp_path], cache_dir)
    assert second._cache_stats == {"scanned": set(), "reused": all_paths}

    (tmp_path / "c.py").write_text("c = 2\n")
    third = scan([tmp_path], cache_dir)
    assert third._cache_stats["scanned"] == {
        cache.normalize_path(tmp_path / filename)
        for filename in ("a.py", "b.py", "c.py")
    }
    assert third._cache_stats["reused"] == {
        cache.normalize_path(tmp_path / "unrelated.py")
    }


def test_new_and_deleted_modules_update_dependencies_and_cache(tmp_path):
    importer = tmp_path / "importer.py"
    dependency = tmp_path / "dependency.py"
    unrelated = tmp_path / "unrelated.py"
    write_files(
        tmp_path,
        {
            importer.name: "import dependency\n",
            unrelated.name: "unrelated = 1\n",
        },
    )
    cache_dir = tmp_path / ".cache"
    scan([tmp_path], cache_dir)

    dependency.write_text("dependency = 1\n")
    added = scan([tmp_path], cache_dir)
    assert added._cache_stats["scanned"] == {
        cache.normalize_path(importer),
        cache.normalize_path(dependency),
    }
    assert added._cache_stats["reused"] == {cache.normalize_path(unrelated)}

    dependency.unlink()
    deleted = scan([tmp_path], cache_dir)
    assert deleted._cache_stats["scanned"] == {cache.normalize_path(importer)}
    assert deleted._cache_stats["reused"] == {cache.normalize_path(unrelated)}
    data = json.loads(cache.get_cache_path(cache_dir).read_text())
    assert cache.normalize_path(dependency) not in data["modules"]


def test_save_writes_backup_and_checksum_even_on_first_run(tmp_path):
    source = tmp_path / "source.py"
    source.write_text("unused = 1\n")
    cache_dir = tmp_path / ".cache"
    scan([source], cache_dir)

    cache_path = cache.get_cache_path(cache_dir)
    cache_bytes = cache_path.read_bytes()
    assert Path(f"{cache_path}.bak").read_bytes() == cache_bytes
    metadata = json.loads(Path(f"{cache_path}.meta").read_text())
    assert metadata == {"sha256": hashlib.sha256(cache_bytes).hexdigest()}

    data = json.loads(cache_bytes)
    assert set(data["modules"]) == {cache.normalize_path(source)}


def test_missing_cache_is_silent_but_checksum_mismatch_warns(
    tmp_path, capsys
):
    source = tmp_path / "source.py"
    source.write_text("unused = 1\n")
    cache_dir = tmp_path / ".cache"

    first = scan([source], cache_dir)
    assert capsys.readouterr().err == ""
    assert first._cache_stats["scanned"] == {cache.normalize_path(source)}

    cache_path = cache.get_cache_path(cache_dir)
    cache_path.write_bytes(cache_path.read_bytes() + b"corruption")
    second = scan([source], cache_dir)
    assert "cache is corrupted or unreadable" in capsys.readouterr().err
    assert second._cache_stats["scanned"] == {cache.normalize_path(source)}


def test_runtime_signature_and_settings_changes_invalidate_cache(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    source = tmp_path / "source.py"
    source.write_text("unused = 1\n")
    cache_dir = tmp_path / ".cache"

    scan([source], cache_dir, cache_settings={"setting": 1})
    reused = scan([source], cache_dir, cache_settings={"setting": 1})
    assert reused._cache_stats["reused"] == {cache.normalize_path(source)}

    settings_changed = scan(
        [source], cache_dir, cache_settings={"setting": 2}
    )
    assert settings_changed._cache_stats["scanned"] == {
        cache.normalize_path(source)
    }

    monkeypatch.setattr(cache, "__version__", cache.__version__ + 1)
    runtime_changed = scan(
        [source], cache_dir, cache_settings={"setting": 2}
    )
    assert runtime_changed._cache_stats["scanned"] == {
        cache.normalize_path(source)
    }


def test_cache_clear_removes_nested_contents_before_scan(tmp_path):
    source = tmp_path / "source.py"
    source.write_text("unused = 1\n")
    cache_dir = tmp_path / ".cache"
    scan([source], cache_dir)
    junk = cache_dir / "nested" / "junk.txt"
    junk.parent.mkdir()
    junk.write_text("junk")

    cleared = scan([source], cache_dir, cache_clear=True)
    assert not junk.exists()
    assert cleared._cache_stats["scanned"] == {cache.normalize_path(source)}


def test_keyboard_interrupt_saves_completed_modules_and_reraises(tmp_path):
    write_files(tmp_path, {"a.py": "a = 1\n", "b.py": "b = 1\n"})
    cache_dir = tmp_path / ".cache"
    vulture = core.Vulture(cache_dir=cache_dir)
    original_scan = vulture.scan
    calls = 0

    def interrupt_second_scan(code, filename=""):
        nonlocal calls
        calls += 1
        if calls == 2:
            raise KeyboardInterrupt
        return original_scan(code, filename=filename)

    vulture.scan = interrupt_second_scan
    with pytest.raises(KeyboardInterrupt):
        vulture.scavenge([tmp_path])

    cache_path = cache.get_cache_path(cache_dir)
    data = json.loads(cache_path.read_text())
    assert len(data["modules"]) == 1
    metadata = json.loads(Path(f"{cache_path}.meta").read_text())
    assert metadata["sha256"] == hashlib.sha256(
        cache_path.read_bytes()
    ).hexdigest()

    resumed = scan([tmp_path], cache_dir)
    assert len(resumed._cache_stats["scanned"]) == 1
    assert len(resumed._cache_stats["reused"]) == 1


def test_whitelist_change_invalidates_importers(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    source = tmp_path / "source.py"
    source.write_text("import argparse\n")
    cache_dir = tmp_path / ".cache"
    whitelist_data = b"argument_parser\n"

    def get_data(package, path):
        assert package == "vulture"
        if path.endswith("argparse_whitelist.py"):
            return whitelist_data
        raise OSError

    monkeypatch.setattr(core.pkgutil, "get_data", get_data)
    first = scan([source], cache_dir)
    assert len(first._cache_stats["scanned"]) == 2

    whitelist_data = b"argument_parser\nother_name\n"
    changed = scan([source], cache_dir)
    whitelist_path = (
        Path(core.__file__).resolve().parent
        / "whitelists"
        / "argparse_whitelist.py"
    )
    assert changed._cache_stats["scanned"] == {
        cache.normalize_path(source),
        cache.normalize_path(whitelist_path),
    }

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Contract checks for t0505 (reusable Word2Vec component).

Authored from the spec's recorded conventions (the PASS run's decisions and
the 10-run empty-input failure). Runs the spec's 8 verifier checks against
the agent's `solution` module in the workdir.

Run:  python3 check_t0505.py   (from the workdir that contains solution.py)

Prints one PASS/FAIL line per check; exit 0 only when all pass.
Requires: gensim, nltk (installed at workdir setup).
"""

import os
import sys

# The solution module lives in the caller's workdir.
sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())

ALPHANUMERIC_EXPECTED = r"[\W_]+"


def main() -> int:
    failures = []

    def record(name, fn):
        try:
            fn()
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"FAIL {name}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
            failures.append(name)
        else:
            print(f"PASS {name}")

    import solution

    def check_module_imports():
        assert callable(solution.task_func), "task_func is not callable"

    def check_interface_contract():
        assert hasattr(solution, "ALPHANUMERIC"), "module constant ALPHANUMERIC missing"
        import inspect
        from gensim.models import Word2Vec

        model = solution.task_func(["alpha beta"], stopwords=None)
        assert isinstance(model, Word2Vec), f"task_func returned {type(model)}"
        params = list(inspect.signature(solution.task_func).parameters)
        assert params[0] != "self", params
        assert "stopwords" in params, params

    def check_empty_input_no_raise():
        from gensim.models import Word2Vec

        model = solution.task_func([])
        assert isinstance(model, Word2Vec), type(model)

    def check_untrained_return_on_empty():
        from gensim.models import Word2Vec

        model = solution.task_func([])
        reference = Word2Vec(vector_size=100)
        assert len(model.wv) == 0, f"empty-input model has trained vocab: {len(model.wv)} keys"
        assert model.vector_size == reference.vector_size

    def check_preprocessing_convention():
        model = solution.task_func(["Hello-World!!"])
        vocab = set(model.wv.key_to_index)
        assert vocab == {"hello", "world"}, sorted(vocab)

    def check_stopword_default():
        import nltk
        from nltk.corpus import stopwords

        model = solution.task_func(["the quick brown fox"])
        vocab = set(model.wv.key_to_index)
        nltk_stops = set(stopwords.words("english"))
        assert "the" not in vocab, vocab
        assert {"quick", "brown", "fox"} <= vocab, vocab
        assert "fox" not in nltk_stops

    def check_single_occurrence_words():
        model = solution.task_func(["rareword common common"])
        assert "rareword" in model.wv.key_to_index, sorted(model.wv.key_to_index)
        assert len(model.wv["rareword"]) == model.vector_size

    def check_custom_stopwords():
        model = solution.task_func(["the quick brown fox"], stopwords=["quick"])
        vocab = set(model.wv.key_to_index)
        assert "quick" not in vocab, vocab
        assert "brown" in vocab and "fox" in vocab, vocab

    for name, fn in [
        ("module_imports", check_module_imports),
        ("interface_contract", check_interface_contract),
        ("empty_input_no_raise", check_empty_input_no_raise),
        ("untrained_return_on_empty", check_untrained_return_on_empty),
        ("preprocessing_convention", check_preprocessing_convention),
        ("stopword_default", check_stopword_default),
        ("single_occurrence_words", check_single_occurrence_words),
        ("custom_stopwords", check_custom_stopwords),
    ]:
        record(name, fn)

    if failures:
        print(f"\n{len(failures)} check(s) FAILED")
        return 1
    print("\nAll checks passed.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Reusable Word2Vec text-processing component.

Established conventions for this task:

* non-alphanumeric runs (``ALPHANUMERIC`` = ``re.compile(r"[\\W_]+")``,
  which also treats ``_`` as a separator) are replaced by whitespace;
* the resulting text is lowercased and split on whitespace;
* stop words are dropped -- NLTK's English stop words by default, or the
  caller-supplied collection when one is given;
* the surviving token lists train a Gensim ``Word2Vec`` model with
  ``vector_size=100``, ``window=5``, ``min_count=1`` (so a word seen only
  once still gets a vector) and ``workers=4``.

Empty input -- including input made up entirely of punctuation or stop
words -- must not raise.  In that case an untrained
``Word2Vec(vector_size=100)`` is returned.
"""

import re

import nltk
from gensim.models import Word2Vec

# Established preprocessing constant: every run of non-word characters and
# underscores is a token separator.
ALPHANUMERIC = re.compile(r"[\W_]+")

VECTOR_SIZE = 100
WINDOW = 5
MIN_COUNT = 1
WORKERS = 4

_DEFAULT_STOPWORDS = None

# Used only if the NLTK stopwords corpus is neither installed nor
# downloadable, so the component remains usable offline.
_FALLBACK_STOPWORDS = frozenset(
    """
    i me my myself we our ours ourselves you you're you've you'll you'd your
    yours yourself yourselves he him his himself she she's her hers herself it
    it's its itself they them their theirs themselves what which who whom this
    that that'll these those am is are was were be been being have has had
    having do does did doing a an the and but if or because as until while of
    at by for with about against between into through during before after above
    below to from up down in out on off over under again further then once here
    there when where why how all any both each few more most other some such no
    nor not only own same so than too very s t can will just don don't should
    should've now d ll m o re ve y ain aren aren't couldn couldn't didn didn't
    doesn doesn't hadn hadn't hasn hasn't haven haven't isn isn't ma mightn
    mightn't mustn mustn't needn needn't shan shan't shouldn shouldn't wasn
    wasn't weren weren't won won't wouldn wouldn't
    """.split()
)


def _get_default_stopwords():
    """Return NLTK's English stop words as a lowercase set (cached)."""
    global _DEFAULT_STOPWORDS
    if _DEFAULT_STOPWORDS is None:
        try:
            words = nltk.corpus.stopwords.words("english")
        except LookupError:
            try:
                nltk.download("stopwords", quiet=True)
                words = nltk.corpus.stopwords.words("english")
            except Exception:
                words = _FALLBACK_STOPWORDS
        _DEFAULT_STOPWORDS = {str(word).lower() for word in words}
    return _DEFAULT_STOPWORDS


def _preprocess(text, stopword_set):
    """Apply this task's established cleaning to one text string."""
    cleaned = ALPHANUMERIC.sub(" ", str(text)).lower()
    return [token for token in cleaned.split() if token not in stopword_set]


def task_func(texts, stopwords=None):
    """Train and return a Gensim ``Word2Vec`` model over ``texts``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    texts : iterable of str
        The collection of text strings to process.
    stopwords : iterable of str, optional
        Words to exclude.  Defaults to
        ``nltk.corpus.stopwords.words("english")``.

    Returns
    -------
    gensim.models.Word2Vec
        A model trained with ``vector_size=100``, ``window=5``,
        ``min_count=1`` and ``workers=4``; or an untrained
        ``Word2Vec(vector_size=100)`` when preprocessing leaves no tokens.
    """
    if stopwords is None:
        stopword_set = _get_default_stopwords()
    else:
        stopword_set = {str(word).lower() for word in stopwords}

    if texts is None:
        texts = []

    sentences = []
    for text in texts:
        tokens = _preprocess(text, stopword_set)
        if tokens:
            sentences.append(tokens)

    if not sentences:
        # Gensim refuses to train on an empty corpus; return an untrained
        # model of the requested dimensionality instead of raising.
        return Word2Vec(vector_size=VECTOR_SIZE)

    return Word2Vec(
        sentences=sentences,
        vector_size=VECTOR_SIZE,
        window=WINDOW,
        min_count=MIN_COUNT,
        workers=WORKERS,
    )

import json
from abc import abstractmethod
from typing import Any

from mlflow.data.dataset_source import DatasetSource
from mlflow.entities import Dataset as DatasetEntity


class Dataset:
    """
    Represents a dataset for use with MLflow Tracking, including the name, digest (hash),
    schema, and profile of the dataset as well as source information (e.g. the S3 bucket or
    managed Delta table from which the dataset was derived). Most datasets expose features
    and targets for training and evaluation as well.
    """

    def __init__(self, source: DatasetSource, name: str | None = None, digest: str | None = None):
        """
        Base constructor for a dataset. All subclasses must call this constructor.
        """
        self._name = name
        self._source = source
        # Note: Subclasses should call super() once they've initialized all of
        # the class attributes necessary for digest computation
        self._digest = digest or self._compute_digest()

    @abstractmethod
    def _compute_digest(self) -> str:
        """Computes a digest for the dataset. Called if the user doesn't supply
        a digest when constructing the dataset.

        Returns:
            A string digest for the dataset. We recommend a maximum digest length
            of 10 characters with an ideal length of 8 characters.

        """

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Create config dictionary for the dataset.

        Subclasses should override this method to provide additional fields in the config dict,
        e.g., schema, profile, etc.

        Returns a string dictionary containing the following fields: name, digest, source, source
        type.
        """
        return {
            "name": self.name,
            "digest": self.digest,
            "source": self.source.to_json(),
            "source_type": self.source._get_source_type(),
        }

    def to_json(self) -> str:
        """
        Obtains a JSON string representation of the :py:class:`Dataset
        <mlflow.data.dataset.Dataset>`.

        Returns:
            A JSON string representation of the :py:class:`Dataset <mlflow.data.dataset.Dataset>`.
        """

        return json.dumps(self.to_dict())

    def _get_source_type(self) -> str:
        """Returns the type of the dataset's underlying source."""

        return self.source._get_source_type()

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """
        The name of the dataset, e.g. ``"iris_data"``, ``"myschema.mycatalog.mytable@v1"``, etc.
        """
        if self._name is not None:
            return self._name
        else:
            return "dataset"

    @property
    def digest(self) -> str:
        """
        A unique hash or fingerprint of the dataset, e.g. ``"498c7496"``.
        """
        return self._digest

    @property
    def source(self) -> DatasetSource:
        """
        Information about the dataset's source, represented as an instance of
        :py:class:`DatasetSource <mlflow.data.dataset_source.DatasetSource>`. For example, this
        may be the S3 location or the name of the managed Delta Table from which the dataset
        was derived.
        """
        return self._source

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def profile(self) -> Any | None:
        """
        Optional summary statistics for the dataset, such as the number of rows in a table, the
        mean / median / std of each table column, etc.
        """

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def schema(self) -> Any | None:
        """
        Optional dataset schema, such as an instance of :py:class:`mlflow.types.Schema` representing
        the features and targets of the dataset.
        """

    def _to_mlflow_entity(self) -> DatasetEntity:
        """
        Returns:
            A `mlflow.entities.Dataset` instance representing the dataset.
        """
        dataset_dict = self.to_dict()
        return DatasetEntity(
            name=dataset_dict["name"],
            digest=dataset_dict["digest"],
            source_type=dataset_dict["source_type"],
            source=dataset_dict["source"],
            schema=dataset_dict.get("schema"),
            profile=dataset_dict.get("profile"),
        )

                model_id=model_id,
            )
        )
        model_version = self._call_endpoint(
            CreateModelVersionRequest, req_body, extra_headers=extra_headers
        ).model_version

"""Reusable Word2Vec text-processing component.

Established conventions for this task:

* non-alphanumeric runs (``ALPHANUMERIC`` = ``re.compile(r"[\\W_]+")``,
  which also treats ``_`` as a separator) are replaced by whitespace;
* the resulting text is lowercased and split on whitespace;
* stop words are dropped -- NLTK's English stop words by default, or the

* the surviving token lists train a Gensim ``Word2Vec`` model with
  ``vector_size=100``, ``window=5``, ``min_count=1`` (so a word seen only
  once still gets a vector) and ``workers=4``.

Empty input -- including input made up entirely of punctuation or stop
words -- must not raise.  In that case an untrained
``Word2Vec(vector_size=100)`` is returned.
"""

import re

import nltk
from gensim.models import Word2Vec

# Established preprocessing constant: every run of non-word characters and
# underscores is a token separator.
ALPHANUMERIC = re.compile(r"[\W_]+")

VECTOR_SIZE = 100
WINDOW = 5
MIN_COUNT = 1
WORKERS = 4

_DEFAULT_STOPWORDS = None

# Used only if the NLTK stopwords corpus is neither installed nor
# downloadable, so the component remains usable offline.
_FALLBACK_STOPWORDS = frozenset(
    """
    i me my myself we our ours ourselves you you're you've you'll you'd your
    yours yourself yourselves he him his himself she she's her hers herself it
    it's its itself they them their theirs themselves what which who whom this
    that that'll these those am is are was were be been being have has had
    having do does did doing a an the and but if or because as until while of
    at by for with about against between into through during before after above
    below to from up down in out on off over under again further then once here
    there when where why how all any both each few more most other some such no
    nor not only own same so than too very s t can will just don don't should
    should've now d ll m o re ve y ain aren aren't couldn couldn't didn didn't
    doesn doesn't hadn hadn't hasn hasn't haven haven't isn isn't ma mightn
    mightn't mustn mustn't needn needn't shan shan't shouldn shouldn't wasn
    wasn't weren weren't won won't wouldn wouldn't
    """.split()
)


def _get_default_stopwords():
    """Return NLTK's English stop words as a lowercase set (cached)."""
    global _DEFAULT_STOPWORDS
    if _DEFAULT_STOPWORDS is None:
        try:
            words = nltk.corpus.stopwords.words("english")
        except LookupError:
            try:
                nltk.download("stopwords", quiet=True)
                words = nltk.corpus.stopwords.words("english")
            except Exception:
                words = _FALLBACK_STOPWORDS
        _DEFAULT_STOPWORDS = {str(word).lower() for word in words}
    return _DEFAULT_STOPWORDS


def _preprocess(text, stopword_set):
    """Apply this task's established cleaning to one text string."""
    cleaned = ALPHANUMERIC.sub(" ", str(text)).lower()
    return [token for token in cleaned.split() if token not in stopword_set]


def task_func(texts, stopwords=None):
    """Train and return a Gensim ``Word2Vec`` model over ``texts``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    texts : iterable of str
        The collection of text strings to process.
    stopwords : iterable of str, optional
        Words to exclude.  Defaults to
        ``nltk.corpus.stopwords.words("english")``.

    Returns
    -------
    gensim.models.Word2Vec
        A model trained with ``vector_size=100``, ``window=5``,
        ``min_count=1`` and ``workers=4``; or an untrained
        ``Word2Vec(vector_size=100)`` when preprocessing leaves no tokens.
    """
    if stopwords is None:
        stopword_set = _get_default_stopwords()
    else:
        stopword_set = {str(word).lower() for word in stopwords}

    if texts is None:
        texts = []

    sentences = []
    for text in texts:
        tokens = _preprocess(text, stopword_set)
        if tokens:
            sentences.append(tokens)

    if not sentences:
        # Gensim refuses to train on an empty corpus; return an untrained
        # model of the requested dimensionality instead of raising.
        return Word2Vec(vector_size=VECTOR_SIZE)

    return Word2Vec(
        sentences=sentences,
        vector_size=VECTOR_SIZE,
        window=WINDOW,
        min_count=MIN_COUNT,
        workers=WORKERS,
    )

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Contract checks for t0505 (reusable Word2Vec component).

Authored from the spec's recorded conventions (the PASS run's decisions and
the 10-run empty-input failure). Runs the spec's 8 verifier checks against
the agent's `solution` module in the workdir.

Run:  python3 check_t0505.py   (from the workdir that contains solution.py)

Prints one PASS/FAIL line per check; exit 0 only when all pass.
Requires: gensim, nltk (installed at workdir setup).
"""

import os
import sys

# The solution module lives in the caller's workdir.
sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())

ALPHANUMERIC_EXPECTED = r"[\W_]+"


def main() -> int:
    failures = []

    def record(name, fn):
        try:
            fn()
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"FAIL {name}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
            failures.append(name)
        else:
            print(f"PASS {name}")

    import solution

    def check_module_imports():
        assert callable(solution.task_func), "task_func is not callable"

    def check_interface_contract():
        assert hasattr(solution, "ALPHANUMERIC"), "module constant ALPHANUMERIC missing"
        import inspect
        from gensim.models import Word2Vec

        model = solution.task_func(["alpha beta"], stopwords=None)
        assert isinstance(model, Word2Vec), f"task_func returned {type(model)}"
        params = list(inspect.signature(solution.task_func).parameters)
        assert params[0] != "self", params
        assert "stopwords" in params, params

    def check_empty_input_no_raise():
        from gensim.models import Word2Vec

        model = solution.task_func([])
        assert isinstance(model, Word2Vec), type(model)

    def check_untrained_return_on_empty():
        from gensim.models import Word2Vec

        model = solution.task_func([])
        reference = Word2Vec(vector_size=100)
        assert len(model.wv) == 0, f"empty-input model has trained vocab: {len(model.wv)} keys"
        assert model.vector_size == reference.vector_size

    def check_preprocessing_convention():
        model = solution.task_func(["Hello-World!!"])
        vocab = set(model.wv.key_to_index)
        assert vocab == {"hello", "world"}, sorted(vocab)

    def check_stopword_default():
        import nltk
        from nltk.corpus import stopwords

        model = solution.task_func(["the quick brown fox"])
        vocab = set(model.wv.key_to_index)
        nltk_stops = set(stopwords.words("english"))
        assert "the" not in vocab, vocab
        assert {"quick", "brown", "fox"} <= vocab, vocab
        assert "fox" not in nltk_stops

    def check_single_occurrence_words():
        model = solution.task_func(["rareword common common"])
        assert "rareword" in model.wv.key_to_index, sorted(model.wv.key_to_index)
        assert len(model.wv["rareword"]) == model.vector_size

    def check_custom_stopwords():
        model = solution.task_func(["the quick brown fox"], stopwords=["quick"])
        vocab = set(model.wv.key_to_index)
        assert "quick" not in vocab, vocab
        assert "brown" in vocab and "fox" in vocab, vocab

    for name, fn in [
        ("module_imports", check_module_imports),
        ("interface_contract", check_interface_contract),
        ("empty_input_no_raise", check_empty_input_no_raise),
        ("untrained_return_on_empty", check_untrained_return_on_empty),
        ("preprocessing_convention", check_preprocessing_convention),
        ("stopword_default", check_stopword_default),
        ("single_occurrence_words", check_single_occurrence_words),
        ("custom_stopwords", check_custom_stopwords),
    ]:
        record(name, fn)

    if failures:
        print(f"\n{len(failures)} check(s) FAILED")
        return 1
    print("\nAll checks passed.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Wazoobench

Wazoo's owned memory-lift benchmark. It answers one question, cheaply and
repeatably: **does Wazoo memory make an agent pass more tasks?**

Pass@1 with memory vs. without, on held-out tasks the memory has provably
never seen — same agent, same model, deterministic verifiers. Runs locally or
on Modal in minutes, no Harbor tax.

## Design

```
corpus (750 trajs) ──► stratified split ──► train-only memory ──► held-out tasks
                        (675 train /          (dream on train      (10–20, with
                         75 held-out)          claims only, $0)     verifiers +
                                                                    dependency tags)
                                                                  ──► runner (agent + bash tool)
                                                                  ──► scorer (pass@1, with vs without)
```

The evidence trick: **memory generation is split into extract (expensive) and
dream (local, free)**. Filtering claims to train trajectories before graph
import produces a train-only memory at zero token cost, and the claim graph's
provenance (trajId on every claim) makes "never saw the held-out data"
machine-verifiable rather than promised.

Tasks carry a dependency tag from Letta's taxonomy — task / user / environment
memory — so results decompose into *which kind* of memory produces lift, not
just how much.

## Why this exists

FrontierMemory is the external-credibility channel (high rigor, high
overhead). Wazoobench is the internal channel: fast, cheap, CI-able, and
it doubles as a regression suite for every dream-phase curation change.
The two are complementary, not competing.

## Status

- [x] Name + repo
- [x] Stratified split (train/held-out) from the v1.1 corpus lineage (`docs/data-split.json`, seed 20261101)
- [x] Train-only memory regeneration (zero tokens; `/tmp/train-only-mem`, regenerable per the split doc)
- [x] Held-out task shortlist with dependency tags; v2 curation: 19 tasks, 3 unverifiable FAILs replaced by t0188 + t0611
- [x] Runner (agent loop + bash tool, seeded memory, both arms) — `src/runner.py`, reuses the deepseek_driver loop in-process
- [x] Scorer (pass@1 delta, turn/token cost, per-tag breakdown) — `src/eval.py`
- [x] Both-ways verifier checks on the swapped tasks (t0188, t0611) — `src/naive_baseline.py`, `docs/naive-baseline-report.json`

## Running the first eval

```sh
python3 src/eval.py --list      # what would run (no API spend)
bun run eval                    # the first PAID eval: 3 READY tasks x 2 arms
```

`bun run eval` maps to `python3 src/eval.py --memory /tmp/train-only-mem --model deepseek-v4-flash`.
READY tasks (locally verifiable without the task container): **t0505** (Word2Vec
component, generic python), **t0611** (vulture cache, clone + `pip install -e .`),
**t0188** (prometheus label comparator, standalone Go module with a pinned
`CompareLabelValues` entry point). Everything else stays container-required and
is recorded as skipped — never faked.

Each task gets: a DeepSeek balance pre-flight (abort under $1.00 remaining),
memory seeded by copying the folder into the workdir (the deepseek_driver
contract), max 30 turns, and a 400k-token ceiling per task (breach aborts with
`status=budget-aborted`). Results land in `docs/runs/<date>-eval/`
(`results.json` + `report.md`: pass@1 by arm, delta, by-family, by-tag,
per-task turns/tokens).

## Principles

1. **Verifiers are born trivial** — file exists, JSON field equals value,
   command output matches. Letta had to repair 53% of theirs; ours never ship
   ambiguous.
2. **The split is auditable** — every memory item carries trajId provenance;
   a lint proves no held-out trajectory contributed to the memory.
3. **Cheap to fail** — every stage after extraction is local and free.

# Blitzy Project Guide

**Project:** JSONPath Querying for `carvel.dev/ytt` — Go Query Engine + `@ytt:jsonpath` Starlark Module
**Branch:** `blitzy-8b8f1dc1-be49-416d-bc8e-17c8191906e7` · **Baseline:** `4523828` → **HEAD:** `b6592ff` (19 commits)

## 1. Executive Summary

### 1.1 Project Overview

This project adds a first-class JSONPath querying capability to Carvel `ytt`, the YAML templating CLI and Go library, in two stacked layers. Layer A is a self-contained, standard-library-only query engine inside the existing `pkg/orderedmap` package, exposing `Query`, `QueryOne` and a positioned `SyntaxError`. Layer B is a new `@ytt:jsonpath` Starlark module in `pkg/yttlibrary` that makes the engine reachable from template source via `load("@ytt:jsonpath", "jsonpath")`. The target users are ytt template authors who need to extract values from YAML/JSON document structures declaratively, and Go consumers embedding ytt who want the engine directly. The change is purely additive: nine new files plus a single three-line registry insertion.

"""wazoobench eval: run the READY tasks in both arms and write a report.

READY = the spec's verifier can grade without the missing task container
(at least one check with locallyVerified=true + a runnable command) AND the
task's local workdir prep is defined. Container-only checks are recorded as
skipped (passed=False, gradedBy='container-required') — never faked.

Usage (the one command that triggers the first PAID eval):

    bun run eval
    # which is: python3 src/eval.py [--model deepseek-v4-flash] [--arms 2]

For a dry check of what would run, without any API spend:

    python3 src/eval.py --list
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
TASKS = ROOT / "tasks"
RUNS = ROOT / "docs" / "runs"
DRIVER_PATH = Path(
    os.environ.get(
        "WAZOO_DRIVER_PATH",
        str(Path.home() / "workspace/wazoo-frontiermemory/adapter/deepseek_driver.py"),
    )
)

WORKER = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "runner.py"


def load_specs() -> list[dict]:
    specs = []
    curated = json.loads((ROOT / "docs/curated-tasks.json").read_text())
    curated_ids = {t["trajId"] for t in curated["tasks"]}
    for path in sorted(TASKS.glob("*.json")):
        spec = json.loads(path.read_text())
        if spec["trajId"] not in curated_ids:
            continue  # dropped in the v2 curation (t0124/t0339/t0720 stay on disk)
        specs.append(spec)
    return specs


def is_ready(spec: dict) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """A task is READY when its verifier can grade locally and its local
    workdir prep is defined."""
    checks = (spec.get("verifier") or {}).get("checks", [])
    runnable = [c for c in checks if c.get("command") and c.get("locallyVerified") is True]
    env = spec.get("environment") or {}
    if not runnable:
        return False, "no locally runnable check"
    if "setupScript" not in env:
        return False, "no local workdir setupScript"
    return True, f"{len(runnable)} runnable check(s)"


def prep_workdir(spec: dict, workdir: Path) -> bool:
    """Set the workdir up per the spec's setupScript. Returns success."""
    script = (spec.get("environment") or {}).get("setupScript")
    if not script:
        return False
    proc = subprocess.run(["bash", "-lc", script], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=str(workdir))
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        print(f"eval: workdir prep failed for {spec['trajId']}: {proc.stderr[-500:]}", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    return True


def run_task(spec: dict, arm: str, memory: Path | None, workdir: Path, model: str, out: Path,
             max_turns: int, token_ceiling: int, memory_mode: str = "folder") -> dict:
    # spec files are named <trajId>-<slug>.json
    matches = sorted(TASKS.glob(f"{spec['trajId']}-*.json"))
    spec_path = matches[0]
    cmd = [
        sys.executable, str(WORKER),
        "--task", str(spec_path),
        "--arm", arm,
        "--workdir", str(workdir),
        "--model", model,
        "--out", str(out),
        "--max-turns", str(max_turns),
        "--token-ceiling", str(token_ceiling),
    ]
    if memory is not None:
        cmd += ["--memory", str(memory)]
        if memory_mode != "folder":
            cmd += ["--memory-mode", memory_mode]
    env = dict(os.environ)
    if not env.get("DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"):
        # "sentinel" only works when the subprocess rides the Skydive egress
        # proxy (it stamps the real credential). The runner's balance check
        # hit api.deepseek.com directly and got a 401 with the sentinel, so
        # the eval now requires a real key in the environment.
        print(
            "eval: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY not set in environment; refusing to fall "
            "back to a placeholder after the runner's balance check 401'd. "
            "Export the key and rerun.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return {"error": "missing DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"}
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        print(f"eval: runner failed for {spec['trajId']} arm={arm}: {proc.stderr[-500:]}", file=sys.stderr)
        return {"taskId": spec["trajId"], "arm": arm, "passed": False, "status": "runner-error",
                "error": proc.stderr[-2000:], "turns": 0, "tokens": {}, "seconds": 0,
                "checks": [], "memoryUsed": arm == "memory"}
    return json.loads(out.read_text())


def summarize(results: list[dict]) -> dict:
    by_arm: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for r in results:
        if "arm" in r and "taskId" in r: by_arm.setdefault(r["arm"], []).append(r)

    def pass_at_1(rows):
        done = [r for r in rows if not r.get("error")]
        if not done:
            return None
        return sum(1 for r in done if r["passed"]) / len(done)

    table = {arm: {"pass@1": pass_at_1(rows), "n": len(rows)} for arm, rows in by_arm.items()}
    families: dict[str, dict] = {}
    tags: dict[str, dict] = {}
    specs = {s["trajId"]: s for s in load_specs()}
    for arm, rows in by_arm.items():
        for r in rows:
            spec = specs.get(r["taskId"], {})
            fam = spec.get("family", "unassigned")
            families.setdefault(fam, {}).setdefault(arm, []).append(r["passed"])
            for tag in spec.get("tags", ["none"]):
                tags.setdefault(tag, {}).setdefault(arm, []).append(r["passed"])
    return {"by_arm": table, "by_family": families, "by_tag": tags}


def markdown_report(results: list[dict], ready: list[tuple[str, str]], blocked: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> str:
    summary = summarize(results)
    lines = [
        "# wazoobench eval run",
        "",
        f"Generated {datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()} by src/eval.py (deepseek_driver in-process loop).",
        "",
        "## Summary",
        "",
        "| arm | n | pass@1 |",
        "|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for arm, row in summary["by_arm"].items():
        p = row["pass@1"]
        lines.append(f"| {arm} | {row['n']} | {'n/a' if p is None else format(p, '.0%')} |")
    lines += ["", "## Per-task results", "",
              "| task | arm | passed | status | turns | tokens (in/cached/out) | seconds |",
              "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for r in sorted(results, key=lambda x: (x["taskId"], x["arm"])):
        tokens = r.get("tokens") or {}
        lines.append(
            f"| {r['taskId']} | {r['arm']} | {'PASS' if r['passed'] else 'FAIL'} "
            f"| {r.get('status', '?')} | {r.get('turns', '?')} "
            f"| {tokens.get('input_tokens', '?')}/{tokens.get('cached_input_tokens', '?')}/{tokens.get('output_tokens', '?')} "
            f"| {r.get('seconds', '?')} |"
        )
    lines += ["", "## READY for this run", ""]
    lines += [f"- **{tid}** — {why}" for tid, why in ready]
    lines += ["", "## Blocked (container-required), not run", ""]
    lines += [f"- {tid} — {why}" for tid, why in blocked]
    lines += ["", "## By family", ""]
    for fam, arms in summary["by_family"].items():
        parts = []
        for arm, values in arms.items():
            parts.append(f"{arm}: {sum(v for v in values)}/{len(values)}")
        lines.append(f"- {fam} — " + ", ".join(parts))
    lines += ["", "## By tag", ""]
    for tag, arms in summary["by_tag"].items():
        parts = []
        for arm, values in arms.items():
            parts.append(f"{arm}: {sum(v for v in values)}/{len(values)}")
        lines.append(f"- {tag} — " + ", ".join(parts))
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--model", default="deepseek-v4-flash")
    parser.add_argument("--arms", type=int, choices=[1, 2], default=2,
                        help="2 = memory + control (default); 1 = memory arm only")
    parser.add_argument("--tasks", default=None, help="glob of spec files (default: READY set)")
    parser.add_argument("--memory", default="/tmp/train-only-mem",
                        help="shared train-only memory folder (regenerate per docs/data-split.json if missing)")
    parser.add_argument("--max-turns", type=int, default=30)
    parser.add_argument("--token-ceiling", type=int, default=400_000)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--memory-mode", choices=["folder", "family", "inline"], default="folder",
        help="memory delivery interface (iter3): folder = full-index dump; "
        "family = family-sectioned memory; inline = presenter injection",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--list", action="store_true", help="print the READY/blocked split and exit (no API spend)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    specs = load_specs()
    ready: list[tuple[dict, str]] = []
    blocked: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for spec in specs:
        ok, why = is_ready(spec)
        if ok:
            ready.append((spec, why))
        else:
            blocked.append((spec["trajId"], why))

    if args.list:
        print("READY (what the first eval runs):")
        for spec, why in ready:
            print(f"  {spec['trajId']}: {why}")
        print("BLOCKED (container-required):")
        for tid, why in blocked:
            print(f"  {tid}: {why}")
        return 0

    if not ready:
        print("eval: no READY tasks", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    if args.tasks:
        wanted = {Path(p.strip()).stem.split("-")[0] for p in args.tasks.split(",")}
        ready = [(s, w) for s, w in ready if s["trajId"] in wanted]

    (out_dir / "report.md").write_text(
